title: A CI pipeline, stage by stage
summary: Stages, jobs that wait for each other, and conditions: how a pipeline decides what runs.

text: On each push, the CI server runs your pipeline: jobs grouped in stages.
- Stages run one after the other.
- Jobs in the same stage run side by side: unit and lint together.
- A job fails? The next stages don't run.
On GitLab, .gitlab-ci.yml lists the stages; each job picks one.
- A job's stage must be in that list, spelled the same.
- rules decide when a job exists. Here: only on main, and someone must click.
On GitHub Actions, jobs run side by side unless you say otherwise.
- needs: test makes deploy wait for test, and skip if test fails.
- if: keeps it to the main branch.
- Without needs, a broken build can still deploy!

scheme: PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DB }}   ✔ kept by the CI
text: Everyone who can read the repository reads the pipeline file, and its history forever.
- Keep secrets in the CI settings: secrets on GitHub, CI/CD variables on GitLab.
- A secret committed by mistake must be changed, not only deleted.
